main.title: The Eye of Judgment
main.subtitle: Place a card on the table and watch it appear
main.summary: The Eye of Judgment is Sony's PlayStation 3 card-battle game, first released in North America on 23 October 2007. A PlayStation Eye camera watches physical cards placed on a printed three-by-three playmat, recognising their codes and presenting their creatures on the television. The player handles an ordinary card while the game supplies the animated battle and its rules. The arrangement makes the table part of the console's playfield. A strategic choice has a visible physical location, connecting the card in the player's hand to the creature occupying a space on screen.

cards.heading: Place a card on the table and watch it appear
cards.text: The Eye of Judgment is Sony's PlayStation 3 card-battle game, first released in North America on 23 October 2007. A PlayStation Eye camera watches physical cards placed on a printed three-by-three playmat, recognising their codes and presenting their creatures on the television. The player handles an ordinary card while the game supplies the animated battle and its rules. The arrangement makes the table part of the console's playfield. A strategic choice has a visible physical location, connecting the card in the player's hand to the creature occupying a space on screen.

cards.heading: Five occupied spaces decide the contest
cards.text: The objective is to occupy five of the nine fields, making control of the small board more important than simply attacking every opposing creature. Players take turns introducing creatures and spells, choosing where each card can best contribute. The camera reads the placement, so the orientation and position of a physical object belong to the digital match. A small number of spaces keeps the whole contest visible at once. The challenge comes from recognising which field matters next and which card should be committed to holding or contesting it.

cards.heading: A camera bundled with a different kind of game
cards.text: The release helped introduce the PlayStation Eye, with bundles including the camera, stand, mat and cards needed to establish the tabletop view. Further sets arrived in 2008, expanding the collection and associated systems. The hardware gives the game a particularly clear purpose for image recognition: it connects a physical collection to a rules-driven animated contest. Instead of using the camera mainly to show the player, The Eye of Judgment asks it to recognise the player's decisions on the table and bring those decisions into the world displayed by the console.

main.title: Ratchet & Clank Future: Tools of Destruction
main.subtitle: A new galaxy for an old partnership
main.summary: Ratchet & Clank Future: Tools of Destruction is Insomniac Games' PlayStation 3 platform shooter, released in North America on 23 October 2007. Emperor Tachyon's attack sends Ratchet and Clank into a journey connected to the Lombaxes and their disappearance. The pair travel between planets, gathering weapons and gadgets as the story begins the series' Future saga. Familiar jumping and shooting return in larger, more detailed surroundings. Ratchet remains the main playable character, with Clank supplying both practical abilities and a mystery that the adventure gradually brings forward.

cards.heading: A new galaxy for an old partnership
cards.text: Ratchet & Clank Future: Tools of Destruction is Insomniac Games' PlayStation 3 platform shooter, released in North America on 23 October 2007. Emperor Tachyon's attack sends Ratchet and Clank into a journey connected to the Lombaxes and their disappearance. The pair travel between planets, gathering weapons and gadgets as the story begins the series' Future saga. Familiar jumping and shooting return in larger, more detailed surroundings. Ratchet remains the main playable character, with Clank supplying both practical abilities and a mystery that the adventure gradually brings forward.

cards.heading: Find a use for an unlikely weapon
cards.text: Ratchet's arsenal turns combat into a choice between conspicuously different effects. A weapon that works well against a group may serve another purpose when an enemy keeps its distance. Using equipment develops it, encouraging the player to return to a favourite tool while trying newly purchased additions. Bolts gathered around the levels fund that growing collection. Movement between battles includes jumping, gliding and gadget-assisted traversal, so a planet provides more than another arena: it also asks how Ratchet's changing equipment can carry him through its obstacles.

cards.heading: A controller that tilts the route
cards.text: Some weapons and movement sections use the SIXAXIS controller's tilt sensing, including sequences where Ratchet falls through the air. These passages briefly change the physical action asked of the player without abandoning the adventure's established controls. Brian Allgeier directed the game, with David Bergeaud continuing his work on the series' music. Critics welcomed the presentation and familiar mixture of platforming and comic weaponry. The ending left the partners' story open, leading into Quest for Booty and then A Crack in Time on PlayStation 3.

main.title: Zack & Wiki: Quest for Barbaros' Treasure
main.subtitle: A pirate adventure made of small puzzles
main.summary: Zack & Wiki: Quest for Barbaros' Treasure is Capcom's Wii adventure about an aspiring pirate and his monkey companion. A talking skull promises them treasure in exchange for recovering the scattered parts of its cursed owner, Captain Barbaros. Each stage places a treasure chest beyond a sequence of obstacles that must be understood and manipulated. Pointing directs Zack through the scene, while the Wii Remote performs the actions required by discovered tools. The adventure combines the observation of a graphic adventure with objects that ask to be used physically.

cards.heading: A pirate adventure made of small puzzles
cards.text: Zack & Wiki: Quest for Barbaros' Treasure is Capcom's Wii adventure about an aspiring pirate and his monkey companion. A talking skull promises them treasure in exchange for recovering the scattered parts of its cursed owner, Captain Barbaros. Each stage places a treasure chest beyond a sequence of obstacles that must be understood and manipulated. Pointing directs Zack through the scene, while the Wii Remote performs the actions required by discovered tools. The adventure combines the observation of a graphic adventure with objects that ask to be used physically.

cards.heading: An enemy can become the missing tool
cards.text: Ringing Wiki like a bell transforms nearby creatures into useful objects. A centipede can become a saw, creating a practical connection between the inhabitants of a scene and the obstacle blocking progress. Using the resulting item changes the view and asks the player to mimic its operation with the Remote. Sawing, turning and pouring therefore become parts of the solution rather than separate decorative gestures. The challenge is to recognise what the scene contains, understand what it could become and use that transformation at the right point.

cards.heading: A solved chest still rewards a cleaner attempt
cards.text: Successful actions earn HirameQ points, with the reward affected by the difficulty and the number of attempts needed. Reaching the chest completes a stage after Wiki removes the spirits guarding it, and the resulting grade encourages another attempt with a better understanding of the sequence. The pirate hideout offers access to collected treasures and items that can provide hints or another chance after failure. These systems give the short stages a longer life, allowing an awkward first discovery to become a much more confident performance on a return visit.

main.title: Final Fantasy Tactics A2: Grimoire of the Rift
main.subtitle: A book opens onto Ivalice
main.summary: Final Fantasy Tactics A2: Grimoire of the Rift is Square Enix's Nintendo DS tactical role-playing game about Luso Clemens, a boy drawn into Ivalice through a magical book. He joins a clan led by Cid and searches for a way home while becoming involved in its disputes and missions. Battles unfold on isometric grids, where the composition of the group matters before the first move. The book supplies the reason for entering another world; the clan provides a practical place within it, with work to accept and companions to develop.

cards.heading: A book opens onto Ivalice
cards.text: Final Fantasy Tactics A2: Grimoire of the Rift is Square Enix's Nintendo DS tactical role-playing game about Luso Clemens, a boy drawn into Ivalice through a magical book. He joins a clan led by Cid and searches for a way home while becoming involved in its disputes and missions. Battles unfold on isometric grids, where the composition of the group matters before the first move. The book supplies the reason for entering another world; the clan provides a practical place within it, with work to accept and companions to develop.

cards.heading: A job changes what a unit can do
cards.text: The Job system gives clan members different combat roles and abilities. Equipment and development shape those choices, allowing the player to prepare a party for the demands of a mission. On the battlefield, position determines which targets and spaces can be reached during a turn. A well-built unit still needs a useful place to stand. The combination connects long-term character growth to short-term spatial decisions, so preparing a clan is not separate from its tactical life. It is the beginning of the next plan.

cards.heading: Work within the law
cards.text: Battles can impose laws that restrict particular actions, requiring the player to adapt an otherwise comfortable approach. The rule gives a familiar group another problem to solve without replacing its abilities. Beyond the active party, clan members can be sent on training assignments or side missions, allowing the organisation to keep developing. Tactics A2 makes a substantial adventure from this routine of accepting work, preparing people and meeting conditions. Luso's search for home runs through a world in which a clan's everyday decisions create the substance of the journey.

main.title: Golden Joystick Awards 2007
main.summary: The Golden Joystick Awards, with every category winner of the 2007 edition.

cards.heading: The players' awards
cards.text: The Golden Joystick Awards celebrate games through a public vote, bringing players into the choice of each year's winners. The awards began in Britain with the 1983 season and later reached an international audience through online voting. Their changing categories trace the growth of games: home computers and consoles, handhelds, online play, independent studios, performance and music. Alongside the public vote, special honours recognise individual contributions to the industry. Each edition preserves its own category names, so the results also show what players and the awards organisers considered worth celebrating at the time.

main.title: Guitar Hero III: Legends of Rock
main.subtitle: Neversoft turns the guitar duel into a rock spectacle
main.summary: The first Neversoft Guitar Hero mixed familiar note highways with a cooperative career, online competition and battles against guitar icons.

cards.heading: A new studio takes the stage
cards.text: Guitar Hero III: Legends of Rock launched in North America on October 28, 2007. Neversoft took over the principal development role after Harmonix’s earlier games; other studios handled particular versions. The game kept the five-colour note highway and guitar-controller performance while building a career around increasingly demanding venues and songs. Its 73 playable songs mix original recordings and covers. A separate cooperative career gives two players lead and bass or rhythm parts, while several console versions also offered online competition.

cards.heading: Turning a solo into a duel
cards.text: The new Battle mode lets opponents disrupt one another rather than simply compare scores. Special note sequences award attacks that can interfere with the other player’s instrument or performance, making familiar musical patterns suddenly harder to read. Slash and Tom Morello appear as opponents, linking the plastic-guitar fantasy to recognisable performers. These theatrical confrontations sit alongside the more direct satisfaction of following a riff accurately, maintaining a streak and finally surviving a difficult solo.

main.title: Naruto: Rise of a Ninja
main.subtitle: A familiar village becomes somewhere to explore
main.summary: Naruto: Rise of a Ninja is Ubisoft Montreal's Xbox 360 action-adventure, released in North America on 30 October 2007. It follows the early anime story through Naruto's development as a young ninja, combining an explorable three-dimensional environment with one-on-one fighting. The player crosses rooftops, completes tasks and earns money for improvements before entering encounters presented through a more focused combat system. The cel-shaded characters and locations connect those activities to the animated series, allowing the village to function as a place the player learns rather than simply a background behind successive fights.

cards.heading: A familiar village becomes somewhere to explore
cards.text: Naruto: Rise of a Ninja is Ubisoft Montreal's Xbox 360 action-adventure, released in North America on 30 October 2007. It follows the early anime story through Naruto's development as a young ninja, combining an explorable three-dimensional environment with one-on-one fighting. The player crosses rooftops, completes tasks and earns money for improvements before entering encounters presented through a more focused combat system. The cel-shaded characters and locations connect those activities to the animated series, allowing the village to function as a place the player learns rather than simply a background behind successive fights.

cards.heading: Travel and fighting develop together
cards.text: Platforming and races test Naruto's movement through the environment, while encounters shift into a fighting-game arrangement of attacks, combinations and special moves. New abilities expand the available responses as the story progresses. The player returns to familiar places with a greater command of the character, connecting improvement in combat to the broader adventure. Tasks and upgrades give exploration a practical purpose between major confrontations. This alternation keeps the story moving through different kinds of activity: understanding a route across the village can matter before the next opponent needs to be defeated.

cards.heading: A Western studio adapts the early anime
cards.text: Rise of a Ninja was the first Naruto game developed by a non-Japanese company and drew specifically on the English-dubbed anime. Its adventure covers the story through the Invasion of Konoha arc. A separate fighting mode offered local contests and Xbox Live competition, with downloadable characters expanding the roster after release. Ubisoft followed it with The Broken Bond in 2008. The original's distinctive choice was to place familiar fighting encounters inside a navigable world, giving the player time to inhabit Naruto's surroundings between the events and rivalries that define the series.

main.title: Super Mario Galaxy
main.summary: Super Mario Galaxy is a 2007 platform game developed and published by Nintendo for the Wii.

cards.heading: Mario among small planets
cards.text: Super Mario Galaxy is a 2007 platform game developed and published by Nintendo for the Wii. It is the third 3D platformer game in the Super Mario series. As Mario, the player embarks on an extraterrestrial mission to rescue Princess Peach and save the universe from his arch-nemesis Bowser, after which the player can play the game as Luigi for a more challenging experience. The levels consist of galaxies filled with minor planets, asteroids, and worlds, with different variations of gravity, the central element of gameplay. The player-character is controlled using the Wii Remote and Nunchuk and completes missions, fights bosses, and reaches certain areas to collect Power Stars. Certain levels also use the motion-based Wii Remote functions.

cards.heading: From Super Mario 128 to Galaxy
cards.text: Nintendo EAD Tokyo began developing Super Mario Galaxy after the release of Donkey Kong Jungle Beat in late 2004, when Shigeru Miyamoto suggested that Nintendo commission a large-scale Mario game. The concept of spherical platforms originated from Super Mario 128, a tech demo for the GameCube shown at Nintendo Space World in 2000. Nintendo aimed to make the game appeal to players of all ages, and the team had more freedom in designing it compared to other Super Mario games because of the outer space setting. The game was directed by Yoshiaki Koizumi and the soundtrack was composed by Mahito Yokota and Koji Kondo, using a symphony orchestra for the first time in the series.

cards.heading: A Wii adventure in 2007
cards.text: Super Mario Galaxy was released on the Wii in Japan on 1 November 2007, with other major territories getting releases for later that month. The game received universal acclaim from critics who lauded its graphics, gravity mechanics, level design, soundtrack, setting, and story. It is the ninth best-selling Wii game worldwide with sales of 12.80 million. The game received a sequel, Super Mario Galaxy 2, in 2010, which also saw similar accolades to its predecessor.

cards.heading: Awards and later editions
cards.text: Galaxy earned multiple Game of the Year awards and became the first Nintendo title to win the BAFTA Award for Best Game. Its gravity-based levels and orchestral score remained central to its reputation. The game later reached additional platforms and appeared in the Nintendo Switch compilation Super Mario 3D All-Stars in 2020.

main.title: Call of Duty 4: Modern Warfare
main.subtitle: When the Military Shooter Changed Eras
main.summary: Infinity Ward moves Call of Duty into a fictional modern conflict, combining a tightly directed campaign with persistent multiplayer progression.

cards.heading: A contemporary Call of Duty
cards.text: Call of Duty 4: Modern Warfare launched in North America on November 5, 2007 for Xbox 360, PlayStation 3 and Windows. Infinity Ward moved from World War II to a fictional contemporary conflict, following British SAS soldiers and U.S. Marines. The campaign alternates assaults with vulnerable moments, while multiplayer links each match to experience, unlocks and custom classes.

cards.heading: Modern equipment changes the fight
cards.text: Night vision, air support and bullets that penetrate light materials change the options available in a firefight. Modern weapons also make some cover less reliable. Studio head Grant Collier described an ambition to reinvent the series while keeping its tightly directed battles. A fictional conflict allowed the campaign to move between several perspectives.

cards.heading: All Ghillied Up
cards.text: All Ghillied Up slows the action as the player follows Captain MacMillan through Pripyat. Staying hidden means watching patrols, measuring distances and remaining still when soldiers pass nearby. Designer Mohammad Alavi described adapting systems and artificial intelligence to support this kind of stealth. The mission draws tension from waiting for the moment when it is safe to move.

cards.heading: A target of sixty frames
cards.text: Infinity Ward targeted 60 frames per second throughout development. The team built performance headroom before adding detail and effects, balancing scene complexity against response and smooth movement. Collier linked that responsiveness to immersion in a 2007 interview. The target shaped which visual effects the game could sustain during combat.

cards.heading: Building a custom class
cards.text: Multiplayer experience levels unlock weapons, attachments and loadout options. Create-a-Class lets players choose equipment for particular ranges and roles, while perks modify abilities such as movement, durability or detection. Progress carries beyond the outcome of a single match, giving players new combinations to try in later sessions.

cards.heading: Three, five and seven kills
cards.text: Three consecutive kills earn a UAV radar, five bring an air strike and seven call in an attack helicopter. These killstreak rewards connect a player's survival to threats and information that affect the entire match. Approaching the next reward raises the pressure to stay alive while opponents respond to the changing map.

cards.heading: Starting again with Prestige
cards.text: After reaching the maximum level, a player can enter Prestige, resetting most unlocks in exchange for a new status symbol. The progression begins again on familiar maps such as Crash, Backlot, Crossfire and Shipment. Their different sightlines and distances support repeated play, while the reset supplies another reason to return.

main.title: Assassin's Creed
main.summary: Assassin's Creed is a 2007 action-adventure game developed by Ubisoft Montreal and published by Ubisoft.

cards.heading: The first Assassin's Creed
cards.text: Assassin's Creed is a 2007 action-adventure game developed by Ubisoft Montreal and published by Ubisoft. It is the first installment in the Assassin's Creed series. The game was released for PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360 in November 2007. A Microsoft Windows version titled Assassin's Creed: Director's Cut Edition containing additional content was released in April 2008.

cards.heading: Desmond enters Alta?r's memories
cards.text: Desmond Miles enters the Animus to relive the memories of his ancestor Altaïr during the Third Crusade in 1191. After a failed mission, Altaïr must regain his standing by finding and killing nine targets across the Holy Land. Their investigations reveal a wider struggle between the Assassins and Templars over freedom, control and powerful artifacts called Pieces of Eden. The modern framing and historical assignments develop together, making each target another step in Altaïr's recovery and another source of information about the conflict.

cards.heading: Crowds, rooftops and the Animus
cards.text: Alta?r explores the cities of Masyaf, Jerusalem, Acre and Damascus using parkour, stealth and counter-based combat. Crowds and the surrounding environment offer ways to hide from guards. Between these memories, the player returns to Desmond inside the Abstergo laboratory, where his captors are seeking information through the Animus.

cards.heading: Reception and Assassin's Creed II
cards.text: Upon release, Assassin's Creed received generally positive reviews, with critics praising its storytelling, visuals, art design, and originality, while criticism mostly focused on the repetitive nature of its gameplay. Assassin's Creed won several awards at the 2006 E3 and several end-year awards after its release. The game spawned two spin-offs: Assassin's Creed: Altaïr's Chronicles (2008) and Assassin's Creed: Bloodlines (2009), which exclude the modern-day aspect and focus entirely on Altaïr. A direct sequel, Assassin's Creed II, was released in November 2009. The sequel continues the modern-day narrative following Desmond but introduces a new storyline set during the Italian Renaissance in the late 15th century and a new protagonist, Ezio Auditore da Firenze. Since the release and success of Assassin's Creed II, subsequent games have been released, with various other Assassins and time periods.
